acts.name: The Wider Wilds
acts.intro: {town}'s name has reached the wider wilds. Seasoned blades come looking for work, and with them come darker stories from farther out.
acts.introDark: The roads beyond the hills are no longer safe for anyone. Those who still come to {town} come armed, and the stories they bring are worse each week.

acts.name: Lords of the Land
acts.intro: Kings write to {town} now, and so do worse things. The powers of the land have noticed the town on the river ford.
acts.introDark: The powers of the land have noticed {town}, and they see it as a prize. Banners nobody wants to see are flying in the far valleys.

acts.name: The Long Night
acts.intro: One enemy has outgrown all the rest. {bigbad} has risen, and the whole of the land waits to see whether {town} will stand.
acts.introDark: The sun comes up grey over {town}. {bigbad} has risen, and there are people in the streets who say it would be easier to kneel.

tribe.rise: Hunters coming down from {region} say {leader} has taken {seat} and is calling every warband in the hills to it.
tribe.riseDark: Hunters coming down from {region} say {leader} has taken {seat}. The bands that answer the call march past burned farms to get there.
strike: Riders of {name} fall on {where} by night and drive off the stock.
A war party of {name} burns the hayricks at {where} and is gone before the bell stops ringing.
Outriders of {name} waylay the carts on the road to {where} and take everything that can be carried.
strikeDark: Riders of {name} fall on {where} by night. They take the stock and leave the barn burning, and someone's body in the lane.
{name} sends a message to {where}: a head on a spear at the crossroads. Everyone knows whose.
tribe.raze: {people} are gone: {name} has burned {settlement} to the ground. The smoke can be seen from the walls.
tribe.slain: {leader} is dead, and the horde breaks apart into quarrelling bands.

undead.rise: The dead are walking out of {region} in long grey lines toward {seat}. Something there called them, and the priests say its name is {leader}.
undead.riseDark: The dead are walking out of {region} toward {seat}, and among them, the shepherds swear, are faces they buried last winter.
strike: Grey shapes from {name} walk into {where} after dark. The watch drives them off with fire, shaking.
Every dog in {where} howls at once at midnight. In the morning the well water tastes of grave dirt.
Something from {name} scratches at the doors of {where} all night, and is gone by first light.
strikeDark: Grey shapes from {name} walk into {where} after dark. In the morning a family is missing, and their door stands open.
The dead of {name} come to {where} for one of their own. The grave they leave behind is empty again by morning.
undead.raze: {people} do not answer the bells any more. {name} has walked through {settlement}, and now its people walk with it.
undead.slain: {leader} crumbles to dust, and across the land the dead lie down again.

schemers.rise: Pedlars from {region} won't say {leader}'s name above a whisper, but they all say it. Bargains are being struck at {seat}.
schemers.riseDark: Pedlars from {region} have stopped coming. The last one smiled too much, and left a gift of {leader}'s at every door.
strike: A pedlar with a too-wide smile sells charms in {where}. By week's end three of the buyers have sickened and the charms are gone.
The milk sours in every pail in {where}, and a stranger's footprints lead from the dairy toward {seat}.
Someone in {where} wakes having signed a paper they do not remember. The ink is red, and the name on it is {leader}'s.
strikeDark: Children in {where} sing a rhyme nobody taught them, about {leader} and the doors that open at night. Two of them walk out of town and are not found.
A woman from {where} trades her shadow to {leader} for her husband's health. He recovers. She is found in the river.
schemers.raze: {people} have struck a bargain with {name}. {settlement} still stands, but its gates are shut to {town} and its people smile at nothing.
schemers.slain: {leader}'s bargains come undone all at once. In {region}, people wake and do not know how long they slept.

dragon.rise: Herders in {region} have seen wings over {seat}. {leader} has claimed it, and the drakes of the high places come when it calls.
dragon.riseDark: Herders in {region} have seen wings over {seat}, and smoke where a farm stood. {leader} has claimed the country, and counts every cow in it as tribute.
strike: {leader} comes down out of {region} at dusk and carries off cattle from {where}, and the drakes take what it leaves.
A shadow crosses {where} at noon. By evening a barn is ash and {leader}'s drakes are picking over the herd.
strikeDark: {leader} burns {where} to the stone, and takes the herdsman with the herd.
{leader}'s fire falls on {where}. The family in the loft did not get out.
dragon.raze: {people} are no more. {leader} burned {settlement} for refusing its tribute.
dragon.slain: {leader} is slain, and its hoard is carried down from {seat} by cart. {region} sees no wings in the sky.

beasts.rise: Trappers in {region} have a name for the thing that has made {seat} its den: {leader}. They no longer set their lines that way.
beasts.riseDark: Trappers in {region} have a name for the thing at {seat}: {leader}. They found what was left of the last ones who went to look.
strike: {leader} comes down out of {region} and takes cattle from {where} in a single night.
Something huge has been at the fences of {where}: posts snapped like kindling, tracks the size of cartwheels.
The herds at {where} stampede at midnight. In the morning half are gone, and {leader}'s cry is heard from the hills.
strikeDark: {leader} comes down out of {region} and tears the roof off a barn in {where}. The farmer's family hid in the root cellar till dawn; the farmer did not.
{leader} takes a shepherd from the hills above {where}, and leaves the crook standing in the snow.
beasts.raze: {people} are no more. {name} has made a hunting ground of {settlement}.
beasts.slain: {leader} is slain, and the wild country of {region} breathes again.

rivals.rise: {leader} has hired every sword in {region} and holds {seat} like a lord. The caravans pay what they're told.
rivals.riseDark: {leader} hangs those who will not pay along the road to {seat}. The caravans pay, and some of them stop coming.
strike: {leader}'s men stop the carts outside {where} and take a third of everything for passage.
Hired blades of {name} rough up the owner of {where} and leave with the till.
{leader}'s agents buy up the grain meant for {where} and sell it back at twice the price.
strikeDark: {leader}'s men stop the carts outside {where}. The carter who argued is left hanging from the milestone as a lesson.
{name} burns {where} for refusing to pay, and posts a notice on the town hall door saying why.
rivals.raze: {people} have bent the knee: {settlement} now flies {leader}'s colours and sends nothing to {town}.
rivals.slain: {leader} is dead, and the free lances melt away to look for a new paymaster.

cult.rise: The singing under {seat} goes on every night now. The priests of {town} say a name the choir answers to: {leader}.
cult.riseDark: The singing under {seat} can be heard from the market square at midnight, and some of the townsfolk hum along without knowing it.
strike: Graves in {town}'s burying ground are found open again, and a lantern burns at {where} that nobody lit.
Hymns nobody knows are chalked on the walls of {where} overnight. The priests scrub them off; they are back by morning.
A procession of hooded figures crosses the fields by {where} at midnight, singing, and does not answer when hailed.
strikeDark: A whole household at {where} walks out at midnight toward {seat}, singing. The watch is told not to follow.
The bell of the shrine rings by itself at {where}, and in the morning the oldest woman in the lane is gone.
cult.raze: {people} of {settlement} have taken the Hollow King's hymn. Their dead do not stay buried, and they say this is a mercy.
cult.slain: {leader} falls silent, and the singing under the hill stops at last.

menaces.powerText: {oldname} has become {name}. {leader} holds {seat} and {holdings} besides, and the lesser lairs of {region} answer the call.
menaces.dominionText: {name} is a power in the land now. {leader} sends heralds and threats the way kings do, and {town} is on the list.
menaces.repelled: Raiders of {name} come for {where}, and {by} drive them off.
menaces.broken: {leader} flees {seat} ahead of the heroes and takes refuge at {refuge}. {name} is broken, but not finished.
menaces.succeeded: {leader} dies at {seat}. {heir} takes up the banner at {refuge}, and {name} fights on.
menaces.rootless: The heroes clear {seat}, but the singing in {town} does not stop. {name} will find another hall.

cunning.name: mindless
cunning.plateau: {name} has grown as large as a thing like that can grow. It hunts; it will never rule.

cunning.name: low cunning
cunning.plateau: {name} has taken all the ground its kind can hold. {leader} is no king: the band squabbles, raids and stays where it is.

cunning.name: mastermind
cunning.domain: Word from {region}: {settlement} now sends tithes to {leader}, and no longer looks to {town}. {name} is patient, and its borders creep outward a valley at a time.

ambitions.name: hunts
ambitions.what: It wants to feed. It raids herds and fields and never thinks past its belly.

ambitions.name: holds its land
ambitions.what: It wants its own ground and nothing more. Leave it be and it keeps to itself; trespass or fail against it and it strikes back.
ambitions.provoked: {name} will not forgive the trespass. {leader}'s creatures are seen on the roads toward {town}.

ambitions.name: conquers
ambitions.what: It wants everything: the land, the peoples of the wilds, and {town}'s walls.

ambitions.name: wants vassals
ambitions.what: It wants {town} kneeling, not burning: a tax and a bent knee. Refuse and it comes to take them.
ambitions.demand: Heralds of {name} ride into {town} under a black banner. {leader} offers peace and protection for a third of the treasury every ten days. Refuse, and the host marches.
ambitions.submitted: {town} bends the knee to {name}. The heralds leave a tax-taker at the town hall, and the raiders stay away.
ambitions.refused: {town} sends the heralds of {name} home with their banner in the mud. {leader} calls the host to arms.

ambitions.name: spreads undeath
ambitions.what: It wants {town}'s people for its own. Its strikes come at night, and the ones it takes do not stay dead.
infect: {victim} of {where} is found pale and cold, two small wounds at the throat. People in {town} bar their windows and whisper about {leader}.
{victim} walks out of {town} after midnight and does not come back. Shepherds say they saw them on the road to {seat}, walking with the dead.
Three graves in {town}'s yard are found open and empty at dawn. {victim} was in one of them, and {leader} has another servant.
ambitions.warded: Something comes to {town} in the night for {victim}, but {by} keeps the door. {leader} goes hungry.

ambitions.name: schemes
ambitions.what: It wants {town} rotten from within: bought councillors, emptied coffers, neighbours at each other's throats.
schemes: Gold goes missing from {town}'s treasury: {gold} gold, and a forged ledger in its place. The trail leads toward {seat}.
Agents of {name} whisper in {town}'s taverns that the mayor sold the town to save their own skin. The Mandate suffers.
A merchant in {town} is found to be in the pay of {leader}. The market sours, and neighbours eye each other.
ambitions.caught: The watch catches an agent of {name} with a satchel of letters. {leader}'s web in {town} loses a strand.

plots.seizedGold: Clearing {site} costs {name} its {asset}: {gold} gold of it comes back to {town}'s treasury.
plots.lieutenant: {lieutenant}, {old}'s lieutenant, slips away from {seat} with the {asset} and the hardest of the survivors. Within a month travellers have a new name to fear.
plots.warned: {contact} in {settlement}, who remembers {memory}, sends word of {leader}'s plan: {plan}

plans.text: {leader} is buying boats and blades to seize the crossing on the road to {settlement}.
plans.done: {name} has seized the road to {settlement} and takes a toll on everything that passes. Caravans there go in fear.
plans.foiled: {leader}'s people try for the road to {settlement}, but the watch there is ready for them and they are driven off.

plans.text: {leader} has sent tithe-takers to {settlement}: gold and cattle, or fire.
plans.done: {settlement} pays {leader}'s tribute. Its people have started calling {leader} their protector.
plans.foiled: {settlement} turns {leader}'s tithe-takers away, and its tower and its band make the refusal stick.

plans.text: {leader} is hunting the other beasts of {region} out of the country it has claimed.
plans.done: Driven out of {region} by {leader}, the beasts of the high places come down toward {town}. {near} is suddenly crowded and hungry.

plans.text: {leader} is building supply camps along the way to {town}.
plans.done: {name} has finished a supply camp at {holding}, and its host eats well.

plans.text: {leader} is gathering ritual components at {seat} for something terrible.
plans.done: The ritual at {seat} is finished. {name} is far stronger than it was.

plans.text: {leader} is buying funeral relics, and has offered {settlement} cheap labour: the dead, to mend its roads.
plans.done: {settlement} has taken {leader}'s dead as workers. Travellers say the living there are no longer allowed to leave.
plans.foiled: {settlement} burns {leader}'s offer and the cart it came in. Its watch has seen what such workers become.

plans.text: {leader} is gathering everything it has for a raid on {town}.
plans.done: {name} is ready. Its raiders are on the move toward {town}.

plans.text: {leader}'s recruiters are working the taverns of {settlement}, where times are hard.
plans.done: Young men and women of {settlement} have gone over to {name}. It is stronger, and {settlement} weaker.
plans.foiled: {leader}'s recruiters leave {settlement} empty-handed: times are too good there for their promises.

feud.taken: Word from {region}: {name} has driven {other} out of {lair} and holds it now.
feud.absorbed: Word from {region}: {other} is no more. {leader} broke it and took its warriors, and {name} grows.

dread.flight: The {family} family load a cart before dawn and take the south road. They do not say goodbye.
dread.desert: {hero} settles the tavern bill and rides out at first light. "This town is finished," they tell the gatekeeper.
dread.refugeesText: {n} survivors of {settlement} reach the gates of {town} with nothing but what they carry.
dread.abandoned: There is no one left who believes. The last families of {town} take the south road together, and the town on the river ford is left to the crows.
toneUp: Unease spreads through {town}. People bar their doors at night who never did before.
A grim mood settles over {town}. The taverns are quiet, and the temple is full.
Darkness gathers over {town}. Some say aloud what many think: that the town is finished.
toneDown: Hope returns to {town}. Children play in the square again, and the bards are back.
The worst seems to be over. {town} starts to rebuild, and to talk about the future.
{town} is grim still, but no longer despairing. People begin to look each other in the eye again.

yoke.sack: The defence collapses. {leader}'s host pours through the breach and puts {town} to the torch. They do not stay: they empty the treasury, hang the town bell in their own hall, and leave a tax-taker at the town hall. {town} is under the yoke of {name}.
yoke.tribute: {name}'s tax-taker counts out {gold} gold from the treasury and rides away with it. Nobody meets anybody's eye.
yoke.missed: {name}'s tax-taker finds the treasury empty. He says nothing, and rides away fast.
yoke.broken: The yoke of {name} is broken! The tax-taker is run out of {town} with the whole market jeering behind him.

finale.crown: {leader} is not satisfied with {region}. {name} sends heralds to every town in the land: kneel, or burn. {town} is the first on the list.

fallback.text: The Old Wyrm who burned the Stonekings has slipped the chains the Smith-King forged for him four thousand years ago.
The ninth mask-queen of Ashkaar, who became a lich rather than die with her empire, has walked out of the Tomb of the Nine Masks.

fallback.leader: the Lord of the Last Door
fallback.text: It sold King Maudren his way past the Ferryman and ended Caldor in a decade. Now it has found another buyer.

finale.fallbackText: Something old wakes in {region}, something that slept through the whole history of {town}. {leader} has risen, and its hunger has a direction.
finale.victory: {leader} is dead. {town}'s heroes come home through cheering crowds, and the second Long Night is over. The bards will be singing about {town} for a hundred years.
finale.victoryDark: {leader} is dead. {town} is half ash and half graves, but it stands, and the morning is clear for the first time in a year.
finale.defeat: {town} falls to {name}. The bards will sing about it, but not in {town}.
finale.march: {name} is on the march! {leader} leads some {army} toward {town}. They will reach the walls in {days} days.
finale.repelled: {town} holds. {leader} draws off with what is left of the host, but {name} is not finished.
finale.escape: {fled} falls, but {leader} is not there to die in it. {Name} slips away to {refuge} and gathers what is left. The Long Night is not over.
finale.regroup: {fled} is cleared, but {leader} got out by a back way before the end. Within the month its servants are creeping back into the ruins. The Long Night is not over.
finale.ride: {heroes} ride out for {seat} to face {leader}. The whole of {town} turns out at the gate to watch them go.

beasts.shape: It walks in on two legs, in a borrowed shape, and only its eyes are its own.

spareText: Beaten at {seat}, {leader} throws down their arms and begs quarter. The heroes spare them, and {leader} swears to serve {town}: against all that {heirs} ever stood for.{shape}
{leader} kneels in the ruin of {seat} and asks to live. The heroes bring them home in chains, and in a month the chains are off. {Heirs} have never bred a turncoat before.{shape}
waverText: {leader} walks out of {seat} alone and unarmed and kneels at {town}'s gate. Nobody knows what changed their heart. {Heirs} call it the worst betrayal in their history.{shape}
A letter comes from {seat} in {leader}'s own hand: they are done with {name}, and they want to fight for {town}. They arrive the next morning, alone.{shape}
fallText: {hero} rides out of {town} one night and does not come back. Everything their past taught them should have held them; it did not.{past}
Something found {hero} in the wilds and spoke to them, and they listened. They leave {town} without a word to their friends.{past}
legendFoe: A stranger asks for the mayor at {town}'s gate and gives the name {name}. In another age, {name} {deed}. Whatever happened between then and now, {name} has come to fight for {town}.
The watch nearly loose their bows at the shape on the road, but it only kneels. It is {name}, who in another age {deed}, and it offers its service to {town}.
legendHero: Old songs know that name. In another age, {name} {deed}. Something in the long dark has changed them.
The oldest folk in {town} go pale at the name. In another age, {name} {deed}, and now they lead the enemy.
